title: Digital Twin for Well-to-Surface Optimization of Cyclic Steam Stimulation (CSS) and Sucker Rod Pump (SRP) Operations for Heavy Oil Wells of Baghewala Field.
description:
• Background Baghewala Field in Rajasthan produces heavy crude oil (17–19° API) from the Jodhpur Sandstone reservoir. The reservoir is characterized by High crude viscosity, High asphaltene content, Low reservoir pressure, Low reservoir temperature (46–48°C) and Poor oil mobility under primary recovery. Consequently, artificial lift and thermal enhanced oil recovery are critical for sustained production. At present, CSS cycle design and SRP operation are optimized separately using historical experience. As reservoir temperature declines after steam injection, crude viscosity increases, leading to reduced pump efficiency, higher energy consumption, rod floating issues, rod failures and lower oil recovery. There is a need for an integrated, data-driven system that continuously optimizes both CSS and artificial lift operations.
• Problem Description Current operations face the following challenges:
• CSS parameters (steam volume, injection pressure, soak time and production cut-off)
are largely based on historical practices.
• SRP operating parameters (stroke length, SPM and VFD settings) are adjusted manually and reactively.
• Heavy crude causes rod floating, impact loading, frequent pump unsetting, rod failures and increased maintenance.
• Reservoir behaviour, wellbore conditions and SRP performance are not optimized together.
• Lack of predictive analytics results in higher Steam-Oil Ratio (SOR), increased energy consumption and reduced production efficiency.
• Expected Outcome / Solution Develop an AI-enabled Well-to-Surface Digital Twin that integrates reservoir, wellbore and surface production systems to provide real-time monitoring, prediction and optimization.
The solution should:
• Optimize CSS cycle parameters.
• Predict reservoir heating, cooling and production performance.
• Continuously optimize SRP operation by adjusting stroke speed and SPM based on well conditions.
• Detect rod floating and minimize impact loading.
• Improve pump efficiency and equipment reliability.
• Optimize steam and energy consumption while reducing operating cost.
• Expected Benefits
• Increased oil production and recovery.
• Reduced Steam-Oil Ratio (SOR).
• Lower energy consumption per barrel.
• Reduced rod failures and pump unsetting.
• Improved equipment life and operational reliability.
• Data-driven and predictive decision making.
• Relevant Data Availability The field has sufficient historical and operational data, including:
• Production history
• CSS cycle records
• Steam injection parameters
• VFD and SRP operating data
• Rod failure and pump unsetting history
• Well completion and reservoir data
• Fluid properties and pressure data
summary: Innovation (5/5): draws on ai, predictive, digital twin applied to a smart automation problem, placing it in the breakthrough band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (2/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Smart Automation. Tech Depth (4/5): centers on api, real-time. Sustainability (4/5): has a clear long-term maintenance path. Scalability (2/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 20/30 -> Yellow verdict.

detail.title: Digital Twin for Well-to-Surface Optimization of CSS and SRP Operations for Heavy Oil Wells

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a system that jointly optimizes steam injection cycles and pump settings for heavy oil wells, connecting the two currently-separate decisions so pump operation actually adapts as steam-heated oil cools and thickens over time, instead of both being tuned by disconnected guesswork.
overview.why_it_matters: Right now steam cycles and pump settings are optimized separately based on historical experience. As the well cools after steam injection, oil thickens and pump efficiency drops, but nothing currently connects these two operations intelligently to respond.
pain_points: CSS cycle parameters (steam volume, pressure, soak time) are based on historical practice, not data-driven optimization.
SRP operating parameters are adjusted manually and reactively as conditions change.
No integrated system connects thermal recovery operations to artificial-lift optimization.
overview.background: Baghewala Field's heavy, viscous crude requires both thermal recovery (CSS) and artificial lift (SRP), but these are currently optimized independently despite being physically coupled, as reservoir cooling after steam injection directly affects pump performance.
overview.whats_being_asked: An integrated, data-driven digital twin continuously optimizing both CSS cycle design and SRP operation together, accounting for the coupling between thermal state and pump performance.
expected_solution: Integrated digital twin modeling both CSS thermal cycles and SRP mechanical operation.
Data-driven optimization connecting steam parameters to pump settings.
Adaptive response to changing viscosity/temperature over the production cycle.
Reduced rod failures and improved recovery efficiency.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Breakthrough. Genuinely coupling thermal reservoir modeling with mechanical pump-system optimization in one integrated digital twin is real petroleum-engineering research territory, not a solved, standard application.
analysis.invention_effort_note: High. Requires real petroleum engineering domain knowledge (thermal recovery physics, sucker-rod-pump mechanics) combined with predictive/optimization modeling, substantial cross-domain depth.

competitive_landscape.note: Extremely specialized petroleum/reservoir engineering domain, requires genuine domain expertise most hackathon teams won't have.

innovation.note: Genuine coupling of thermal and mechanical operations into one optimization system is real, valuable petroleum engineering innovation.

invention.note: Requires real domain understanding of both CSS thermal recovery and SRP mechanics together, substantial specialized depth.

technical_feasibility.note: Real Baghewala Field operational data isn't accessible to a hackathon team; published petroleum engineering literature can ground a credible synthetic approach.

impact_and_benefits.note: Genuine operational value for this specific field's production efficiency, a narrow, specialized industrial audience.

architecture.note: Thermal model, mechanical pump model, and coupled optimization logic together, real cross-domain integration.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Yellow. Genuinely valuable if approached with real petroleum engineering grounding, but requires domain expertise most teams won't have, and real field data isn't accessible. Ground your model in published CSS/SRP petroleum engineering literature rather than inventing physics relationships.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Very well-specified real physical mechanism (thermal cooling affecting viscosity affecting pump load) gives a concrete, physically-grounded coupling to model.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Without real petroleum engineering domain knowledge, a team risks building a superficial data dashboard connecting two unrelated datasets rather than genuinely modeling the real physical coupling.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Research actual published CSS thermal recovery and SRP mechanics literature to ground your coupled model in real petroleum engineering physics, rather than inventing plausible-sounding relationships.

idea_0_4: Research real CSS thermal decline curves and SRP performance-versus-viscosity relationships from published petroleum engineering literature.
Design your coupled model: how does simulated reservoir temperature/viscosity over a CSS cycle map to required SRP parameter adjustments.
Split: one person on the thermal/CSS model, one on the SRP mechanical model.
prototype_4_22: Build your CSS thermal decline model based on real published relationships.
Build your SRP performance model responding to changing simulated viscosity.
Start connecting the two, so SRP recommendations adapt as your CSS model's simulated temperature declines.
integration_22_30: Test your coupled system across a full simulated CSS cycle, confirming SRP recommendations genuinely change as temperature/viscosity evolves.
Build the optimization layer suggesting parameter adjustments (stroke length, SPM) based on current coupled state.
Add rod-failure-risk flagging based on load conditions your model predicts.
polish_30_36: Build a clear dashboard showing the coupled thermal-mechanical state over a simulated cycle.
Rehearse explaining the real physical coupling your model represents and its grounding in published research.
Prepare to discuss what real Baghewala Field data validation would require.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Show your SRP recommendation genuinely and correctly shifting as your simulated CSS thermal cycle progresses, e.g. recommending adjusted stroke length as viscosity increases post-injection, that responsive coupling, grounded in real petroleum engineering relationships, is the actual point of this PS.

strengths: Very well-specified, physically real coupling mechanism gives concrete modeling direction.
Genuine operational value if approached with real domain grounding.
weaknesses: Requires real petroleum engineering domain knowledge most hackathon teams won't have.
Real field data isn't accessible, synthetic grounding in published literature is essential.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: This PS needs genuine petroleum engineering domain knowledge, without it, the coupling model risks being superficial.
team_fit.approach: Research real CSS and SRP engineering relationships thoroughly before building any model.

ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Correctly modeling the real thermal-mechanical physical coupling based on genuine petroleum engineering principles, that requires real domain expertise.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: An AI-scaffolded model connecting two datasets without genuine physical grounding in real CSS/SRP engineering relationships would produce plausible-looking but physically meaningless coupling.

data_resource_availability.status: Real Baghewala Field operational data isn't accessible to a hackathon team; published petroleum engineering research on CSS thermal decline and SRP mechanics provides credible grounding.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Build a synthetic model grounded in real, cited petroleum engineering literature, clearly labeled as synthetic but scientifically grounded.

judge_qna.question: What real petroleum engineering research grounds your thermal-mechanical coupling model?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Cite the specific published research on CSS thermal decline and SRP performance-viscosity relationships your model is based on, don't present the coupling as self-evident.
judge_qna.follow_up: How would you validate this against real Baghewala Field data if it became available?

judge_qna.question: How does your system's recommendation change specifically as the reservoir cools post-injection?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Walk through a specific example from your simulation, showing the recommended SRP parameter shift and the physical reasoning (increasing viscosity requiring adjusted stroke/speed) behind it.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's the risk of your model over- or under-correcting compared to real operator judgment?
